cohort: 398,368 women registered via the Free Pre-pregnancy Health Check (FPHC) program from 2017 to 2019 in Hunan Province, China
finding: Pre-pregnancy underweight to some extent is associated with better maternal outcomes, but it has certain adverse effects on neonatal outcomes, while pre-pregnancy overweight, especially obesity, has a substantial adverse effect on pregnancy and perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were lower in the underweight group and higher in the overweight and obese groups compared to the normal BMI group.
